chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from one of his companions, from Aban, from a man, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
There was in the house of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), a pair of red pigeons.
ai.seo_question: What animals were kept in the house of the Prophet Muhammad according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This brief narration from al-Kafi highlights the Prophet’s (peace be upon him and his family) affinity for birds, specifically noting a pair of red pigeons in his home, which serves as evidence for the permissibility and cultural acceptance of keeping pigeons in Islamic tradition. It reflects the simplicity of the Prophet’s domestic environment and aligns with the broader Shia emphasis on the Prophet’s everyday practices (Sunnah) as a model for believers. The mention of specific colors and pairs also underscores the aesthetic and companionable aspects of his household life.
